historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (net revenue) haircut for the Adenza acquisition: FY2024 net revenue +19% carried ~11 months of acquired AxiomSL/Calypso revenue, so the organic run-rate is nearer 8-10% (ARR +12% YoY, Fintech ARR +16% in Q2 2026). Equity CAGR rejected as the anchor: the FY2023 jump (6.2B -> 10.8B) is the ~85M shares issued to Thoma Bravo for Adenza, not retained earnings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (25.6%) diverges >30% from net revenue (13.6%) and EPS (11.0%) because of the Nov-2023 Adenza share issuance; equity CAGR is not a growth signal for this ticker.
historical_growth.notes: All per-share and share-count series are on the post-split basis (3:1 split in 2020): FY2020 EPS $1.89 -> FY2025 $3.12, FY2022 $2.28 -> FY2025 $3.12, so the 3y/5y EPS CAGRs do not span the split boundary. Revenue CAGRs use NET revenue (revenues less transaction-based expenses): FY2020 $2,903M, FY2022 $3,582M, FY2025 $5,249M. Owner-FCF CAGRs: FY2020 $977M and FY2022 $1,448M are reported FCF less the cash-flow SBC add-back only (equity-award tax withholding is not disclosed in the CSV before FY2023), FY2025 $1,755M includes the $69M of equity-award taxes; on a like-for-like SBC-only basis the 3y owner-FCF CAGR is 8.0% and the 5y 13.3%. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (6.6%) sits below reported FCF (8.6%): SBC grew 16%/yr FY2022-25 against 8.6% for reported FCF, so a rising share of the reported growth is being paid in stock, though at 4.5% of net revenue SBC remains modest for a company with a growing software mix.

scenario_narratives.base: Nasdaq completes its transition to a majority-recurring financial-technology and data company. Net revenue grows 13% in FY2026 on an exceptional capital-markets year (SpaceX IPO, record options volumes, record index inflows), then decelerates through 9% to mid-single digits as ARR growth of ~12% (Fintech ~16%) is blended with high-single-digit Market Services and Capital Access growth. GAAP EBITDA margin expands roughly 0.5pt a year from 58% to 61% as software revenue scales against a reinvested cost base. Deleveraging continues and buybacks hold the diluted count flat. The EU antitrust probe resolves without structural remedies.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Adenza thesis compounds: Verafin's consortium network and AxiomSL/Calypso's regulatory embedding drive mid-teens Fintech ARR growth for several more years, index AUM keeps compounding from the $1T mark, the IPO window stays open, and the December-2026 23/5 launch plus 2027 tokenised equities with Kraken add a new Market Services leg. Operating leverage lifts the EBITDA margin to 64% by FY2033, and net revenue roughly 2.3x over the decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026's capital-markets tailwinds reverse in FY2027-28: IPO activity dries up, index AUM and options volumes fall, and off-exchange trading (>50% of Nasdaq-listed volume) keeps eroding cash-equities economics. Fintech bookings slow as big-bank implementations stretch, so ARR growth drops to mid-single digits; the EU antitrust investigation ends in a fine and conduct remedies in Nordic derivatives. Growth settles at ~3% with margins back near 55%, leverage stays near 3x and the capital-return acceleration is paused.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on NET revenue (revenues less transaction-based expenses), SBC and equity-award taxes fully expensed with a flat diluted share count, component-built margins over a 10-year horizon, terminal value the lower of Gordon (3%) and a 20x FCF cap, 8% WACC applied identically across scenarios with risk carried in driver paths and probability weights (20/50/30). Net debt of $8.2B at 2026-06-30 is deducted once; clearing-member default funds and margin deposits are excluded from cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026 base-year anchors (net revenue +13-14%, 58% margin) are struck in a record capital-markets year; a reversal in IPO activity, index AUM or options volumes hits all three segments at once.
EU antitrust investigation (Nordic derivatives, with Deutsche Borse): a fine and conduct remedies are unquantified and sit only in the bear path and bear weight.
~$8.2B of net debt (2.8x EBITDA) from the Adenza deal makes the equity value sensitive to the WACC and terminal assumptions; each 1pt of WACC moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid).
Off-exchange trading migration and SEC market-structure rulemaking could erode Market Services economics faster than the base path assumes.
Terminal value is capped at 20x FCF in base and bull; the cap binds, so the valuation does not assume multiple expansion but does assume the mature business is still worth a compounder multiple.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 76.55-101.79.
data_sources.financials: research/NDAQ/Reports/NDAQ_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL via build_facts_xbrl.py; 10-K FY2025, 10-Q Q2 2026) and the kpis table (buybacks, cash taxes, equity-award taxes, deferred revenue, D&A, interest income).
data_sources.qualitative: research/NDAQ/Reports/NDAQ_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): segments, Q2 2026 results and FY2026 guidance (non-GAAP opex $2.53-2.57B, non-GAAP tax 22.5-24.5%, ARR $3.3B +12%), Adenza deleveraging, EU antitrust probe, 23/5 and tokenisation initiatives.

inputs.revenue_basis: NET revenue (revenues less transaction-based expenses: rebates, brokerage, clearance, exchange fees). This is the CSV 'GrossProfit' column, not the gross 'Revenue' column ($8,262M FY2025), because every margin, opex-guidance and ARR figure Nasdaq publishes is struck on the net basis and gross revenue carries ~$3B of pass-through rebates whose mix is noise. FY2025 net revenue $5,249M; H1-2026 $2,907M (+14.3% YoY).
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average for Q2 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-30), 567.75M; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). A $200-250M ASR announced for Q3 2026 (~2.5M shares) is not yet reflected; buybacks are the mechanism that keeps the count flat, not a separate source of value.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt $8,761M less cash and equivalents $520M at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q). Default funds and margin deposits (clearing-member assets) are excluded from cash, as are restricted cash and the ~$0.2B financial-investments portfolio. Net debt/FY2025 GAAP EBITDA = 2.8x; management's gross-leverage metric was ~3.0-3.1x at late 2025, ahead of the post-Adenza deleveraging schedule.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $165M plus $69M cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities); Nasdaq publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. 4.46% of FY2025 net revenue. Interest income ($39M FY2025) is NOT stripped because the company is a net debtor ($8.2B); it is immaterial against the flows.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $616M; H1-2026 $903M (incl. $548M in Q1), plus a $200-250M ASR announced for Q3 2026. Nasdaq is an active repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a convention it has yet to pay for. Dividends $1.05/share FY2025 (~$600M) are a use of the same owner FCF, not an additional deduction.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 (exchange/market-infrastructure with a growing recurring-software mix) gives cost of equity ~8.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% on the $8.8B of senior notes (after-tax ~3.5%); debt weight ~14% of EV at the current price. Blended ~8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: scenario risk is charged through the driver paths and the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are left inside EBITDA (lease expense is an operating cost in the GAAP income statement; ROU amortisation is not in D&A). Lease liabilities (~$0.5B) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (<$10M); no adjustment.
inputs.da_note: FY2025 D&A $632M = 12.0% of net revenue, of which roughly $440M is amortisation of acquired intangibles (Adenza, Verafin) that runs off and does not scale with revenue. The da_pct path therefore declines from 11.5% toward 7.5% over 10 years (depreciation ~3.5% of revenue grows with the business; amortisation is roughly fixed in dollars). D&A only affects the cash-tax line in the engine; it is added back in full. Cash taxes paid FY2025 $373M (levered) / H1-2026 $284M; a 23.5% rate on EBIT after full D&A reproduces the FY2025 unlevered cash tax within ~$30M and sits inside the guided 22.5-24.5% non-GAAP rate.
inputs.ebitda_note: CSV EBITDA is GAAP operating income + total D&A (FY2025 $2,963M, 56.5% of net revenue; H1-2026 $1,699M, 58.4%). It is AFTER SBC (SBC is subtracted separately in the engine) and after ~$100M/yr of merger, restructuring and strategic-initiative costs that Nasdaq excludes from its non-GAAP figures but which recur every year, so they are left in. Non-GAAP operating margin was 57% in Q2 2026, +2pts YoY.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (FY2026-FY2035), engine route via make build-dcf. Routing: Nasdaq is an operating company (exchange operator + financial-technology software + index/data licensing), not a bank, REIT or LIC; its cash flow statement means what the engine assumes once clearing-member default funds and margin deposits are excluded from cash. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). Valuation date is three quarters into FY2026, so Y1 (FY2026) is largely in hand (H1 net revenue +14.3%); end-of-year discounting of Y1 is the house convention and is mildly conservative here. The EU antitrust investigation (Nordic derivatives, opened Nov 2025 with Deutsche Borse) is unquantified; it is carried in the bear narrative and bear weight rather than as a bridge item. US-domestic USD filer: owner-fcf-adaptations.md not required (no FX, no NCI, no excluded income; single lease treatment stated above).

bear.rationale: FY2026 is largely booked (+12%), then a capital-markets downturn in FY2027-28 (IPO window shuts, index AUM falls, options volumes normalise from records) coincides with off-exchange venues taking further cash-equities share and a slowdown in large-bank Fintech bookings. An EU antitrust fine and conduct remedies on Nordic derivatives land in the margin path (-3pts). Growth settles at 3-3.5% with no operating leverage; Gordon at 2.5% binds below the cap.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +13% (H1 +14.3%, SpaceX IPO and record options volumes in H2 comps; implies H2 ~+12%). Then decelerates from ~9% (ARR +12%, Fintech ARR +16%, Market Services and Capital Access growing high-single digits) toward 4.5% by FY2035 as the Solutions mix matures and the Adenza cross-sell runway is used up.
base.margin_rationale: GAAP EBITDA margin 56.5% FY2025, 58.4% H1-2026; non-GAAP operating margin 57% Q2 2026 (+2pts YoY). Opex guidance raised to $2.53-2.57B for performance comp and marketing, so FY2026 is held at 58.0% rather than extrapolating H1. Thereafter +0.5pt every year or two to 61% as recurring software revenue scales, ~3pts below the bull case.
base.tax_rationale: 23.5% flat on EBIT after full D&A, inside the 22.5-24.5% guided non-GAAP range and reproducing FY2025 unlevered cash tax. As acquired-intangible amortisation runs off the taxable EBIT rises, which the declining da_pct path captures.
base.wc_rationale: Deferred revenue rose $74M on $600M of FY2025 net-revenue growth (12% capture) but other working-capital lines are noisy quarter to quarter; 5% capture on the revenue change is a conservative haircut of the subscription-billing tailwind.

bull.rationale: Fintech ARR sustains mid-teens growth (Verafin cross-sell into 2,800+ institutions, AxiomSL/Calypso regulatory demand, agentic-AI upsell), index AUM compounds from the $1T base, the IPO window stays open, and 23/5 trading plus tokenised equities (NETs, 2027) add incremental Market Services volume. Operating leverage takes the EBITDA margin to 64% by FY2033.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 20% because FY2026 is a cyclical-peak year (record options volumes, the largest IPO in history, record index inflows) that flatters the base-year anchors, and the EU antitrust probe is a live, unquantified regulator risk. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs the capital-markets cycle to stay open AND Fintech ARR to hold mid-teens AND the new initiatives (23/5, tokenisation) to contribute -- several independent things going right. Base at 50%: the recurring-revenue mix shift and deleveraging are well evidenced and the margin path is modest.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
